groups.name: wow
groups.description: The host's configuration, the `wow.*` namespace (decision D110). No key keeps a 9.x meaning; the defaults are the runtime's own. - `wow.service`: the service's name (the lease groups', the wait origins' and the Manifest's), by default `spring.application.name`. - `wow.node.id`, `wow.node.address`: this node's id (by default the host name and a random suffix) and the `host:port` the other nodes reach its internal port at (by default this host's address and `wow.internal.port`). - `wow.internal.port` (9090; 0 for a port the system chooses, which the node learns once bound) and `wow.internal.host` (the host of the node's member address; `0.0.0.0` for every interface, D195): the internal port (D89); `wow.internal.token`, the service's cluster tokens, and `wow.internal.dev-profiles`, the profiles that may go without one (decision D226), see Internal. - `wow.contexts.include`, `wow.contexts.exclude`: the bounded contexts the node serves among the domain modules on the class path, by default all of them (decision D169), see Contexts. - `wow.backend`: `auto` (the default), `memory`, `postgres`, `mongo`, or the type of a community backend's store provider (`me.ahoo.wow.spi.store.StoreProvider`, review R3.3-1); `wow.mongo.database`: the database of a MongoDB store that names none, and `wow.mongo.append-timeout` (5s, decision D261) how long one of its appends' inserts may take, unless its `options.append-timeout` says; `wow.ddl` (`auto`, `validate` or `none`), how the stores manage the framework's tables (review A5-10), `wow.stores.<name>.ddl` per store. - `wow.stores.<name>.*`: the named store instances (decision D177, Store); `wow.log.store` and `wow.snapshot.store`, the stores of the aggregates' logs and snapshots by default; `wow.stores.<name>.query.*`, how its queries run (review R3.4-2, StoreQuery: `max-concurrent`, `read-preference`, `events.unpinned`) and, on PostgreSQL, `wow.stores.<name>.query-data-source`, the `DataSource` bean they read through; per aggregate type, `wow.aggregates.[<context>.<aggregate>].log.store` and `.snapshot.store`. The aggregates whose logs are on one store form a log group, with its own partition sequences, checkpoints, parked entries and timers. Snapshots may have several targets (decision D172, Snapshot): `wow.snapshot.targets` and `wow.snapshot.primary`, per aggregate type `.snapshot.store` as a list and `.snapshot.primary`; `wow.snapshot.interval`, `batch` and `pages` tune the snapshot maintenance, `wow.snapshot.write-batch` how many snapshots of a partition one write holds at most. - `wow.log.partitions` (64; a power of two that divides 4096, decision D240) and `wow.log.append-queue.*` (on, at most 64 appends a group, decision D248); `wow.log.poll-interval` (50ms) and `wow.log.max-poll-interval` (1s), how often the tails of a PostgreSQL or MongoDB log poll: at the first while they find entries, backing off to the second while they find none (finding A2-14). `wow.log.handoff.enabled` (true), `capacity` (1024) and `gap-wait` (1s): the node hands its own commits to its subscriptions' tails in memory (decision D249), which read the store only to catch up: when no append of the node can fill a missing sequence any more (or one that may has not returned within the gap wait), or no commit comes for the longest poll interval. - `wow.cluster.*` (ClusterOptions) and `wow.cluster.router`: `partitioned`, or `local` (the default on the memory backend, which cannot route across nodes). - `wow.wait.default-timeout` (10s), `max-timeout` (60s), `max-hops` (16, at most 32), `unknown-contexts` (`allow` or `reject`, decision D190): the default timeout is the node's (ServiceNodeOptions.defaultWaitTimeout), for every command whose request names none; `max-registered` (16384, review R3.4-3): the waits the node holds at once, beyond which a command that waits past ACCEPTED is not run and is `wow.command.busy`. - `wow.state-views.capacity` (4096), `max-age` (1m), `max-bytes` (64 MiB): the bounds of each context's state views (decision D133), see StateViews. - `wow.executor.lane-capacity` (1024), `wow.executor.max-in-flight` (4096, the node's commands in flight, beyond which a command is `wow.command.busy`, decision D228 ②), `wow.state-cache.capacity` (bounded by a share of the heap in bytes unless set, B.O-4), `wow.state-cache.recent-requests` (256, the requests each cached aggregate keeps of those it committed last, decision D261), `wow.subscription.*`. - `wow.subscriptions.[<subscription>].start`: `beginning`, `end` or an ISO-8601 instant, where the subscription (`processor.function`, bracketed for its dot) starts in a partition it has no checkpoint in yet, instead of its kind's default (decision D154), see SubscriptionSettings. - `wow.subscription.parked.max-retries` (10), `min-backoff` (3m), `execution-timeout` (2m), `scan-interval` (10s): the long-horizon retries of parked entries (roadmap P.1), see Parked; per subscription, `wow.subscriptions.[<subscription>].parked.max-retries`, `min-backoff` and `execution-timeout`, see ParkedSpec. - `wow.subscription.retry.max-attempts` (5), `initial-backoff` (100ms), `max-backoff` (5s), `multiplier` (2.0), `timeout` (none): the in-process retries of a failing handler before its aggregate parks; per subscription, `wow.subscriptions.[<subscription>].retry.*` (roadmap P.3), over the handler's `@Retry`, see RetrySpec. - `wow.subscription.systemic.failing-aggregates` (3, 0 for none), `window` (10s), `initial-backoff` (1s), `max-backoff` (30s): a subscription pauses its partition on a systemic failure (decision D243), or when that many different aggregates failed within the window, and probes it at that backoff until a handling succeeds, see Systemic. A handler's failures are classified by its `@Retry(recoverable, unrecoverable)`, then the `FailureClassifier` beans, the backends' and the runtime's own (decision D229 G-6). - `wow.subscription.backpressure.max-attempts` (20), `initial-backoff` (100ms), `max-backoff` (10s), `jitter` (0.5), `min-concurrency` (1): a handler whose downstream pushes back (`wow.command.busy`, `wow.wait.timeout`, `wow.query.busy`, a 429 with `Retry-After`) is retried with that backoff and jitter while its partition is throttled, then parks; it never pauses the partition (decision D263), see Backpressure. - `wow.ops.enabled` (false): the operator's routes under `/wow/ops/parked`; `wow.ops.webhook.url`, `format` (`generic` or `wecom`), `events` (`parked`, `exhausted`), `timeout` (5s), `headers`: the webhook told when an entry parks or spends its retries, see Ops and Webhook; `wow.ops.publish.enabled` (false), `context` (`ops`), `interval` (30s): the failure ledger published to the ops context (decision D141), see Publish. - `wow.timers.poll-interval` (1s), `lookahead` (30s), `max-attempts` (10), `expires-after` (none), `parallelism` (64), `max-fire-rate` (none, per partition and second), `claim-timeout` (30s), `max-early-wait` (5s): the node's firing loop of the scheduled commands (decision D166), see Timers. - `wow.schedules.<job>.expression`, `zone`, `misfire` (`coalesce` or `catch-up`), `enabled` (true): the host's override of an `@OnSchedule` job's rule (decision D198), see Schedule; a job no handler of the node runs fails its start. - `wow.tenant.default`: the tenant of a caller that has none (D97). - `wow.http.request-facts`, `wow.http.client-facts` (on: `remote_ip` and `user_agent`, personal data that cannot be erased once written), `wow.http.errors.[<code>].status`, `wow.http.global-errors` (on: the application's own routes answer problem+json, review M-3), `wow.http.manifest.enabled`, `wow.http.openapi.enabled` (`GET /wow/openapi`, the OpenAPI document of the routes), `wow.http.openapi.springdoc.enabled` and `group` (the springdoc bridge, decision D233); `wow.http.services.<service>.tokens`: the service identities the internal port trusts without CoSec (decision D193), and `wow.http.services.<service>.commands`, the commands each may call there (decision D226), see Http.Service. - `wow.calls.contexts.<context>.url`, `wow.calls.token`, `wow.calls.timeout` (10s), `wow.calls.connect-timeout` (2s): the synchronous calls of the sagas to other contexts' command gateways (decision D193), see Calls. - `wow.clients.contexts.<context>.url`, `internal-url`, `mode` and `contract` (`jar`, or `manifest` for a peer called by its Manifest alone), `wow.clients.mode` (`service`), `wow.clients.timeout` (30s), `wow.clients.connect-timeout` (2s), `wow.clients.forwarded-headers` (`Authorization`), `wow.clients.retry.max-attempts` (3), `max-retry-after` (5s) and `backoff` (200ms): the typed clients of the peers over HTTP (decisions D257, D259), see Clients. - `wow.aggregates.[<context>.<aggregate>].tenant`: a fixed tenant per aggregate type (decision D116); `wow.aggregates.[<context>.<aggregate>].query.events.unpinned` (`allow` or `refuse`, over its events store's and `wow.query.events.unpinned`; review R3.4-2): whether its `events` queries that name no aggregate run; `wow.aggregates.[<context>.<aggregate>].query.events.store`: the store its `events` queries read (decision D235), its log store when not set, such as an Elasticsearch store whose event search Sink writes its streams; `wow.aggregates.[<context>.<aggregate>].id-generator`: the generator of its new ids (decision D171); `wow.aggregates.[<context>.<aggregate>].routing`: `cluster` (the default, the node's `wow.cluster.router`) or `kafka`, the `Kafka` router (decision D143), see Aggregate. - `wow.cosec.*` and `wow.cosid.*`: the keys wow-cosec and wow-cosid read, see CoSec and CosId. - `wow.health.*` (review R3.5-3): the node's health under Actuator's `wow`, `readiness` and `liveness` groups, when the application has Spring Boot Actuator; `wow.health.enabled` (true), `sample-interval` (10s), `stores.down-after` (15s), `stores.window` (1m), `ownership.handover-grace` (1m), `topics.required` (true), `executor.saturation` (0.9), `subscriptions.lag-degraded-at` (10000), `subscriptions.parked-degraded-at` (100), `liveness.stall-timeout` (3m), see Health. - `wow.topics.in-memory` (false): the node's command topics and published streams in its JVM instead of Kafka, for local development (DX gap G27), see Topics. - `wow.standby` (false): the node starts on standby, for the dual-run window of a migration's cut-over, see standby. Every key is in the host's configuration metadata (`META-INF/spring-configuration-metadata.json`, review A5-9), and a `wow.*` key that no property of the host or of a module names is reported at startup (ConfigurationKeys).

groups.name: wow.calls
groups.description: The synchronous calls of the node's sagas to the command gateways of other contexts (decision D193): each context's base URL (contexts, `wow.calls.contexts.<context>.url`: the target's internal port, `http://host:port` of an address in its internal network, never its public port, which refuses calls), the service token the node presents as `Authorization: Bearer` (token; an application's me.ahoo.wow.client.ServiceCredential bean, such as one that renews a CoSec token, replaces it), how long one call may take (timeout) and connect (connectTimeout). A saga that calls a context without a URL fails, then parks.

groups.name: wow.clickhouse
groups.description: ClickHouse's configuration, `wow.clickhouse.*` (decisions D110, D142, D164), read when wow-clickhouse is on the classpath (ClickHouseAutoConfiguration): - `wow.clickhouse.endpoint`: the server's HTTP endpoint, such as `http://localhost:8123`; ClickHouse is wired only when it is set. `username` (`default`) and `password` (empty) sign in; `database` (`default`) holds the tables. - `wow.clickhouse.sink.enabled`: whether the Manifest's published streams are written to ClickHouse; on by default. - `wow.clickhouse.sink.ddl`: `auto` (create what is missing, then validate; the default), `validate` or `none`. - `wow.clickhouse.sink.batch-size`: the most records one insert carries (1000). - `wow.clickhouse.sink.deduplication-window`: how many recent inserts each table remembers to drop a retried one (1000), the `non_replicated_deduplication_window` of the tables `auto` creates. - `wow.clickhouse.sink.aggregates.<context>.<aggregate>.history.enabled`: whether every commit is kept (on by default); off keeps only the current state. `...history.ttl`: how long the history is kept, forever when unset. - `wow.clickhouse.query.enabled`: whether the datasets are served from ClickHouse (decision D145); on by default. - `wow.clickhouse.query.metadata-ttl`: how long a dataset table's columns and engine are reused before `system.columns` is read again (1m). - `wow.clickhouse.query.settings.<name>`: server settings every dataset query runs under, such as `max_memory_usage`; the execution time comes from each query's budget (`wow.query.http.timeout`), not from here.

groups.name: wow.clients
groups.description: The typed clients of the peer contexts over HTTP (decisions D257, D259), `wow-client`'s: a peer context listed in contexts (one the api jars on the class path declare, decision D234, or one described by its Manifest alone, ClientTarget.contract `manifest`, which takes me.ahoo.wow.client.NamedCommands) is reached over HTTP by the service's me.ahoo.wow.api.client.CommandClient and me.ahoo.wow.api.read.QueryApi beans, in its ClientTarget.mode (or mode); any other context as without these clients (its commands through its topic, review M-1). Where each is: its public routes' base ClientTarget.url (user mode) and its internal port's ClientTarget.internalUrl (service mode; `wow.calls.contexts.<context>.url` when not set, which the sagas' calls use too), or what an application's me.ahoo.wow.client.EndpointResolver bean resolves. Each request is answered within timeout (a command's longer wait aside) after connecting within connectTimeout, and retried as retry says; a user-mode request forwards the forwardedHeaders of the public request it serves. The service mode presents the me.ahoo.wow.client.ServiceCredential bean (`wow.calls.token`).

groups.name: wow.clients.retry
groups.description: How a problem a retry may get past is retried (me.ahoo.wow.client.RetryPolicy).

groups.name: wow.contexts
groups.description: The bounded contexts the node serves (decision D169, ContextSelection): every context of the domain modules on the class path by default; only those include names when set; less those exclude names. A name that is no context on the class path is refused at startup.

groups.name: wow.cosec
groups.description: The keys wow-cosec reads (`wow.cosec.*`), bound here so they are checked and documented as the others are.

groups.name: wow.cosec.cross-scope
groups.description: The callers that may act across scopes: by CoSec role or policy.

groups.name: wow.cosec.service
groups.description: The service identities (decision D193), whose synchronous calls the internal port takes.

groups.name: wow.cosec.tenant-level
groups.description: The tenant-level callers (decision D189), who read and write every aggregate of their tenant.

groups.name: wow.cosid
groups.description: The keys wow-cosid reads (`wow.cosid.*`), bound here as cosec is.

groups.name: wow.health
groups.description: The node's health and its probes (review R3.5-3): `wow.health.*`.

groups.name: wow.health.executor
groups.description: The node's executors (decision D228 ②).

groups.name: wow.health.liveness
groups.description: Whether the node is stuck, so a restart helps; a storage outage never fails it.

groups.name: wow.health.ownership
groups.description: The node's share of each lease group's partitions.

groups.name: wow.health.stores
groups.description: The node's event logs, as its own calls and a probe of their heads see them.

groups.name: wow.health.subscriptions
groups.description: The node's subscriptions, never a reason to take it out of service.

groups.name: wow.health.topics
groups.description: The topics of other contexts the node reads (decision D134).

groups.name: wow.http.openapi.springdoc
groups.description: The springdoc bridge (decision D233), when the application has springdoc.

groups.name: wow.kafka
groups.description: The Kafka transport's configuration, `wow.kafka.*` (decision D110), read when wow-kafka is on the classpath (KafkaAutoConfiguration): - `wow.kafka.bootstrap-servers`: the brokers; the transport, the Kafka Sink and the Kafka-sourced subscriptions are wired only when it is set. - `wow.kafka.properties.*`: passed to every producer and consumer as they are (`security.protocol`, `client.id`, `linger.ms`, ...), except the settings the transport's guarantees rest on (`me.ahoo.wow.kafka.KafkaOptions`). - `wow.kafka.topic-prefix`: put before every topic name, such as `staging.` for `staging.wow.shop.order.state`; none by default, so the topics are the Manifest's (`wow.<context>.<aggregate>.state`, decision D135). The sinks write under it and the subscriptions of other contexts' streams read under it. - `wow.kafka.poll-timeout`: the longest a consumer's poll waits (200 ms by default); a read that is cancelled, and a partition that joins or leaves a topic's shared consumer, take effect within it. - `wow.kafka.offset-gap` (finding A2-11): what a read of another context's topic does when its partition no longer holds the offset it is to read from (the retention deleted it, or the topic was created again): `fail` (the default) fails the read, so the subscription stays where it is, logging errors; to recover, set `earliest` and restart the node. `earliest` reads on from the earliest offset retained; the skipped range is lost to that subscription. Either way the gap is logged as an error and counted (`wow.kafka.offset.gaps`). - `wow.kafka.command-intake`: whether each context the node hosts executes the commands other contexts send to its command topic, `wow.<context>.commands` (decisions D135, D137); off by default. The topic must exist with as many partitions as the context's log, and the node checks it at start. Sending commands to other contexts and reading their receipts need no switch. A context with an aggregate type routed through Kafka (`wow.aggregates.[<context>.<aggregate>].routing=kafka`, decision D143) takes them whatever this says. - `wow.kafka.topics.ddl` (decision D168): how the node manages the topics its contexts own at its start, see Topics: `validate` (the default) fails the start when one is missing or a command topic does not have exactly `wow.log.partitions` partitions; `auto` creates the missing ones first; `none` checks only the command topics the node reads, whose partitions must still be the log's. - `wow.kafka.topics.replication-factor` (the broker's default), `wow.kafka.topics.min-insync-replicas` (the broker's default) and `wow.kafka.topics.configs.*` (`retention.ms`, ...): what `auto` creates a topic with. A command accepted on a command topic is durable only when both are at least 2 (decision D143, review A3-15): at start the node warns when they are below that, as configured or as the command topics of its contexts are, unless a profile of Topics.devProfiles is active (`dev`, `local`, `test`, `demo`). - `wow.kafka.topics.partition-refresh` (30s): how often the node looks for partitions added to the topics it reads (other contexts' streams, its receipts), and its consumers' `metadata.max.age.ms`; the new partitions are read within about twice this.

groups.name: wow.kafka.topics
groups.description: The topics the node's contexts own (decision D168): their DDL, and how `auto` creates them.

groups.name: wow.log.append-queue
groups.description: The partition append queue; each setting not given is the default (AppendQueueOptions): on, 64 a group.

groups.name: wow.log.handoff
groups.description: The hand-over of the node's own commits to its tails in memory (decision D249): a tail waits its gap wait for a missing sequence and maxPollInterval without a commit before it reads the store.

groups.name: wow.opentelemetry
groups.description: Observability's configuration, `wow.opentelemetry.*` (decision D174), read when wow-opentelemetry is on the classpath (ObservabilityAutoConfiguration): - `wow.opentelemetry.enabled`: whether the node is traced and measured; on by default. - `wow.opentelemetry.sample-interval`: how often the gauges that are read, not heard (parked entries, the subscriptions' positions and a rebuild's progress), are sampled (15s).

groups.name: wow.ops
groups.description: The operator's side of the parked entries (roadmap P.1): enabled serves their routes under `/wow/ops/parked` on the public port, off by default; webhook tells a URL when an entry parks or spends its retries.

groups.name: wow.ops.publish
groups.description: Publishing the failure ledger to the ops context (decision D141): when enabled, each entry goes to the `parked` aggregate of context (`ops`) through its command topic, at once when it parks and on a scan every interval (30s); the node needs the Kafka transport.

groups.name: wow.ops.webhook
groups.description: The webhook of the parked entries, posted to url when set: in Wow's JSON (`generic`) or as a WeCom robot's Markdown message (`wecom`) (format), for the events listed (`parked`, `exhausted`; both by default), within timeout, with headers added to each request.

groups.name: wow.query
groups.description: The query plane's configuration, `wow.query.*` (decisions D110, D126, D129, D150, D151), read by QueryAutoConfiguration: - `wow.query.enabled` (true): whether the query routes and gateways are wired at all. - `wow.query.http.*`: the HTTP budget (QueryBudget) every query route runs under: `max-list-size` (1000), `max-page-size` (100), `max-page-window` (10000), `max-filter-nodes` (128), `max-filter-values` (1000), `allow-expensive-operators` (true), `max-residual-groups` (10000), `count-limit` (10000; the bound of a count and of a paged total, D150), `allow-exact-count` (false), `timeout` (30s), `unindexed-sort-expensive` (false); and `default-list-size` (100), the limit of a list that names none. A limit of `0` is off. - `wow.query.in-process.*` (review R4-Q, Q-3): the budget of in-process queries, the typed me.ahoo.wow.api.read.QueryApi's, of trusted code too: the same keys and defaults as `wow.query.http.*`, its `default-list-size` the limit of an in-process list that names none. - `wow.query.in-process-timeout` (30s): the timeout of an in-process query that has no budget, trusted code's that dropped it (`QueryApi.trusted().unbounded()`). - `wow.query.require-explicit-entry`, `wow.query.require-authenticated-scope` (both false): the entry gates. - `wow.query.cross-tenant.enabled` (false; decision D254 ⑦): whether a caller that may act across scopes may query across tenants on the query routes, `Wow-Scope: tenant=*` or `tenant=("t1" "t2")`; 403 `wow.auth.forbidden` while off. A type whose tenant is fixed is still read in that tenant alone, and every such query's audit is logged at INFO (`me.ahoo.wow.query.CrossTenantAudit`). The commands and the state reads never cross tenants. - `wow.query.abac.*` (D129): `enabled` (false), `require-principal-tags` (false), `match-missing-tag-key` (true), `attribute-prefix` (`abac.`): the caller's `abac.<key>` attributes matched against the snapshots' `tags`. - `wow.query.sensitivity.display-comparable` (true): whether filters and sorts may compare a `DISPLAY` value. - `wow.query.index.ddl` (`auto`, `validate` or `none`; D151): how the snapshot backend manages the indexes of each aggregate's `x-wow-index` at startup. - `wow.query.count-cache.*` (D152): `enabled` (true), `max-entries` (10000), `ttl` (30s): the cache of the snapshot counts, valid while the type's snapshot write checkpoint holds and for at most `ttl` (another node's write can make a cached count lag the rows by up to `ttl`); `paged-totals` (false; review R4-Q, Q-12) serves the totals of paged queries from it too, which by default are counted with their page so that a total agrees with its rows; `events-enabled` (false; D259) caches the events' counts the same way, though the log runs ahead of that checkpoint, so a cached events count may lag the streams for up to `ttl`. - `wow.query.dataset.config-directory` (`config`; D75, D145): the working directory whose `wow/dataset/` holds dataset files, `{context}.{dataset}.json`; each takes precedence over the classpath's `META-INF/wow/dataset/` file of the same dataset. The datasets of both are served when a dataset backend is wired (ClickHouse's, say). - `wow.query.memory.enabled` (false; D209): whether the snapshots on a store in memory are queried, from the in-memory reference query backend, and the events of a log in memory, scanned in memory (review R3.4-1): for local runs, demos and tests, not for production. - `wow.query.events.*` (D235): the `events` model, served from each aggregate's log store, or the store its `wow.aggregates.[<context>.<aggregate>].query.events.store` names: `mongo-read-preference` (none, the primary), the MongoDB read preference of its queries (`secondaryPreferred`, say), so a free filter scans a secondary rather than the primary the log appends to; `wow.stores.<name>.query.read-preference` takes its place for one store, and sets that of its snapshot queries too. `unpinned` (`allow`, or `refuse`; review R3.4-2): whether an events query that names no `aggregateId` runs, over which `wow.stores.<name>.query.events.unpinned` and `wow.aggregates.[<context>.<aggregate>].query.events .unpinned` decide for one store or aggregate type; refused, it is `wow.query.invalid` (`STORAGE_UNSUPPORTED` on `aggregateId`), and the model's descriptor lists the constraint `AGGREGATE_REQUIRED`. - `wow.query.dataset.max-concurrent` (8; decision D247): how many dataset queries the node runs at once, under one bulkhead, `datasets`, which keeps the analytics queries from taking a warehouse the Sink writes to; `0` sets none. A query beyond it waits for `wow.query.dataset.max-wait` (`wow.query.max-wait` when unset) in a queue of `wow.query.dataset.max-queued` (`wow.query.max-queued`, else 4 per permit), then is `wow.query.busy`. The bound is fixed, not adaptive (decision D252): the warehouse's writes (the ClickHouse Sink's) give the node no write pressure to adapt to. - `wow.query.max-concurrent` (none: each store's provider derives one from its pool, PostgreSQL a quarter of a pool the appends share, at least 2, or all of a `query-data-source` of its own, 16 otherwise; review R3.4-2): how many snapshot and `events` queries each store runs at once, whichever entry asks, beyond which a query is `wow.query.busy` (429, with `Retry-After`); `wow.stores.<name>.query.max-concurrent` takes its place for one store; `0` for no bound. A query beyond the bound waits in a FIFO queue (decision D247) at most `wow.query.max-wait` (200ms) for a permit, and is refused when the wait runs out or when `wow.query.max-queued` (4 per permit) queries wait already; `wow.stores.<name>.query.max-wait` and `.max-queued` take their place for one store. - `wow.query.adaptive.*` (decision D252, Adaptive): the bound of a store whose `max-concurrent` neither `wow.query.max-concurrent` nor `wow.stores.<name>.query.max-concurrent` fixes adapts to the store's write pressure, evaluated every `interval` (1s): `periods` (2) periods in a row in which its appends' p90 latency is above `latency-factor` (1.5) times its baseline and at least `min-latency` (5ms), or in which `connection-waits` (1) callers wait for a connection of its pool, halve it down to `floor` (1); a calm period in which a query waited or was refused raises it by one up to `ceiling` (none: the provider's, PostgreSQL half a pool the appends share, all of a `query-data-source`'s). `enabled` (true) turns it off; `wow.stores.<name>.query.adaptive.enabled`, `.floor` and `.ceiling` take their place for one store. - `wow.query.state.max-replay` (10000; review R4-Q, Q-1): the most commits a state point read replays from the aggregate's snapshot, or from version 1 (`GET …/state?version=` or `?at=`, `…/state/trace`, the latest state before the first snapshot); a state further away is 400 `wow.query.invalid` (`REPLAY_TOO_LONG`). `min-version-wait` (2s; review R4-Q, Q-13): how long a read of `?minVersion=` (or `QueryApi` state of a minimum version) waits for the aggregate to reach it, its snapshot caught up with its log meanwhile; past it the read is 409 `wow.query.min-version-not-reached` with the current `version`. - `wow.query.stream.*` (decision D253, Stream): a `list` streamed as server-sent events reads keyset chunks of `chunk-size` (500) records, a query permit per chunk, each record's `id` its position; after `max-hold` (30s; `0` for no bound) it ends with `end` `{"reason":"hold-expired","resumable":true}` and the client resumes it with `Last-Event-ID`. Neither `http.max-list-size` nor `http.default-list-size` bounds such a stream. A list whose sort cannot order a cursor streams without positions, under those bounds, and every `end` it sends (the hold time's included) says `"resumable":false`.

groups.name: wow.query.adaptive
groups.description: `wow.query.adaptive.*` (decision D252): how a store's query bound adapts to its write pressure.

groups.name: wow.query.http
groups.description: The budget of the query routes, `wow.query.http.*`.

groups.name: wow.query.in-process
groups.description: The budget of the in-process me.ahoo.wow.api.read.QueryApi, `wow.query.in-process.*`: the HTTP defaults.

groups.name: wow.query.stream
groups.description: `wow.query.stream.*` (decision D253): how a streamed `list` reads its chunks and how long it runs.

groups.name: wow.snapshot
groups.description: Where the snapshots are by default (decision D177): `wow.snapshot.store`.

groups.name: wow.state-views
groups.description: The bounds of each context's state views (decision D133, review A5-10): `wow.state-views.*`.

groups.name: wow.subscription.backpressure
groups.description: How a handler whose downstream pushes back is retried, and its partition throttled (decision D263).

groups.name: wow.subscription.parked
groups.description: How the parked entries are retried over the long horizon (roadmap P.1).

groups.name: wow.subscription.read-retry
groups.description: How a failing read of the log, or write of a store, is retried: until the node stops, the backoff growing for `max-attempts` (5) attempts, after which each failure is logged as an error and retried at `max-backoff` (decision D195).

groups.name: wow.subscription.retry
groups.description: How a failing handler is retried before its entry is parked.

groups.name: wow.subscription.systemic
groups.description: When a partition pauses on a systemic failure (decision D243).

groups.name: wow.timers
groups.description: The node's firing loop of the timers (decisions D166, D198): how often it reads, with one query per timer store over every partition the node owns, the timers due within lookahead (pollInterval); how many attempts a technical failure to send one gets before it is parked under `wow.timers` (maxAttempts); when set, how late a timer may be sent before it expires instead (expiresAfter); how many commands a partition sends at once (parallelism) and, when set, at most a second (maxFireRate), the rate a backlog of overdue timers drains at; how long the claim on a timer being sent holds before another owner may send it (claimTimeout); how long a scheduled command waits in its target for its due time on the target node's clock before it fails instead, to be sent again later (maxEarlyWait).

groups.name: wow.topics
groups.description: The node's topics without Kafka (DX gap G27), see Topics.

properties.name: wow.aggregates
properties.description: Per aggregate type, by `<context>.<aggregate>` (bracketed in a property name: `wow.aggregates.[shop.cart]`).

properties.name: wow.backend
properties.description: The backend of a node that names no `wow.stores` (decision D110): `auto` (the default) takes PostgreSQL or MongoDB by the application's `DataSource` or `MongoClient`, and refuses to start without either (review R3.5-1) unless a profile of `wow.internal.dev-profiles` is active or the internal port binds the loopback interface alone; `memory` keeps the data in memory on purpose, for one node whose data does not outlive it.

properties.name: wow.clickhouse.sink.aggregates
properties.description: By context, then by aggregate name.

properties.name: wow.cluster.forward-timeout
properties.description: How long a forward waits for the owner's reply, capped by the command's own deadline: `wow.wait.default-timeout` when not set (review A5-10), so a node whose waits are longer forwards as long. A forward the owner received and did not answer by then is reported unknown (`wow.command.unknown`), not run here, so a retry with the same request id is safe (decision D223).

properties.name: wow.cluster.reconcile-timeout
properties.description: How long one reconcile may run before the node takes itself as stuck and leaves the members until it ends (finding C.1 F1).

properties.name: wow.cluster.router
properties.description: Where commands run; `local` on the memory backend and `partitioned` on the others when not set.

properties.name: wow.cosec.authorizer.enabled
properties.description: Whether CoSec authorizes every command as its caller (`CoSecCommandAuthorizer`), not only the public routes by path; the services' calls are authorized by CoSec whatever this says (decision D226).

properties.name: wow.cosec.trust-injected-app
properties.description: Whether a service in CoSec's inject mode, behind a CoSec gateway (`cosec.inject.enabled=true` with `cosec.authorization.enabled=false`), records the application of the requests the gateway forwards, their `CoSec-App-Id`, as the caller's app and the request fact `app_id` (decision D236): a trust decision, off by default; in any other mode it fails the startup.

properties.name: wow.cosid.global-generator
properties.description: The CosId generator of the node's global ids (command ids, wait ids); CosId's own `cosid` when not set.

properties.name: wow.ddl
properties.description: How the stores manage the framework's tables, collections and indexes (review A5-10): `auto` creates what is missing (the default), `validate` creates nothing and refuses a store whose schema is missing or in another format, `none` creates and checks nothing; `wow.stores.<name>.ddl` overrides it for one store.

properties.name: wow.executor.lane-capacity
properties.description: The commands one aggregate may have waiting in the executor.

properties.name: wow.executor.max-in-flight
properties.description: The commands the node may have in flight, all contexts together (decision D228 ②): beyond it a command is refused as `wow.command.busy` (429, with `Retry-After`) instead of queued.

properties.name: wow.health.enabled
properties.description: Whether the host contributes the node's health to Actuator and its probe groups.

properties.name: wow.health.executor.saturation
properties.description: The share of `wow.executor.max-in-flight` in flight at which the executor is degraded.

properties.name: wow.health.liveness.stall-timeout
properties.description: How long the node's dispatcher may not tick, or commands in flight not finish while every log answers, before the node is not live.

properties.name: wow.health.ownership.handover-grace
properties.description: How long the owned partitions may differ from the node's share (a hand-over) before the group is degraded, and down (the node not ready) when it owns none of a share that is not empty.

properties.name: wow.health.sample-interval
properties.description: How often the node samples what a probe must not wait for (the logs' heads, the subscriptions' lag and parked entries) and probes its stores.

properties.name: wow.health.stores.down-after
properties.description: How long a log must keep failing, with no success since, before it is down and the node not ready: a failed call or probe, or a probe that timed out (after this long, at least a second); a probe still under way is no failure. `0s` is down at the first failure.

properties.name: wow.health.stores.window
properties.description: A log with a failure this recent is degraded.

properties.name: wow.health.subscriptions.lag-degraded-at
properties.description: The entries a subscription may be behind the log's head before it is degraded.

properties.name: wow.health.subscriptions.parked-degraded-at
properties.description: The parked entries of a subscription, counted up to this, at which it is degraded (as when they grow).

properties.name: wow.health.topics.required
properties.description: Whether a topic the node is still joining makes it not ready; degraded only when false.

properties.name: wow.http.client-facts
properties.description: Whether the public port records each command's client address and `User-Agent` as the request facts `remote_ip` and `user_agent` (09 §17 G-10, as 9.x did), for audit. They are personal data, and written into the event stream, which is never deleted (decision D175): once recorded, they cannot be erased. On by default; off records neither (decision D267 ⑯).

properties.name: wow.http.errors
properties.description: The HTTP status of an error code, by code (bracketed in a property name: `wow.http.errors.[a.b].status`).

properties.name: wow.http.global-errors
properties.description: Answers what fails on the application's own routes as the framework routes' problem+json (review M-3, decision D259): on by default; off leaves those errors to Spring's error handling.

properties.name: wow.http.manifest.enabled
properties.description: Serves `GET /wow/manifest`.

properties.name: wow.http.openapi.enabled
properties.description: Serves `GET /wow/openapi`, the OpenAPI 3.1 document of the routes (roadmap 5a.2).

properties.name: wow.http.openapi.springdoc.enabled
properties.description: Merges the Wow routes into springdoc's documents.

properties.name: wow.http.openapi.springdoc.group
properties.description: The springdoc group of the Wow routes alone: `/v3/api-docs/<group>`.

properties.name: wow.http.request-facts
properties.description: The request headers copied into a command's headers, beside the standard request facts the edge records: `app_id`, the application the caller resolver authenticated (decision D232), and on the public port `user_agent` and `remote_ip` (09 §17 G-10); none of the three can be listed. `remote_ip` is the server's remote address: behind a proxy, set `server.forward-headers-strategy` to have the server take it from the proxy's forwarded headers.

properties.name: wow.http.services
properties.description: The service identities the internal port trusts by their static tokens, by service name (decision D193): a call whose `Authorization: Bearer` token is one of them is that service's, which alone may send `Wow-Call`, and only to the internal port. For a deployment without CoSec; with CoSec, `wow.cosec.service.roles` names its service principals.

properties.name: wow.internal.connect-timeout
properties.description: How long a peer has to accept a connection of the cluster channel or the signal sender.

properties.name: wow.internal.dev-profiles
properties.description: The development profiles, `dev`, `local`, `test` and `demo`: in them the internal port may run without token, and `wow.backend=auto` falls back to memory when no durable backend is available (review R3.5-1).

properties.name: wow.internal.host
properties.description: The address the internal server binds (decisions D173, D195), `0.0.0.0` for every interface; when not set, the host of the member address the node advertises (`wow.node.address`, else this host's address).

properties.name: wow.internal.port
properties.description: The port of the internal server: the cluster channel and the wait signals (decision D89); 0 for one the system chooses, which the node advertises once the server is bound.

properties.name: wow.internal.signal-queue-capacity
properties.description: The signals queued per origin node before they are dropped (decision D109).

properties.name: wow.internal.token
properties.description: The service's cluster tokens (decision D226, review A3-1), at least 32 characters each: the secret its nodes share, which alone opens the cluster channel (`/wow/internal/forward`) and the wait signals of the internal port. A node sends the first and takes any, so a token is rotated by adding the new one second, then moving it first on every node, then removing the old one; a comma-separated value (`WOW_INTERNAL_TOKEN`) is a list. A service token of `wow.http.services` opens the call routes, not these, and this token no call route. A node without one starts only in a profile of devProfiles, or with its internal port bound to the loopback interface alone, and warns: its cluster routes then take every request.

properties.name: wow.kafka.topics.dev-profiles
properties.description: The profiles that run without durable topics, a single broker: no warning about it.

properties.name: wow.log.handoff.gap-wait
properties.description: The longest a tail waits for a missing sequence that an append of the node still in flight may hold; once every such append returned without it, the tail reads the store at once.

properties.name: wow.log.max-poll-interval
properties.description: The longest a tail waits between polls that find nothing: an idle tail backs off up to it.

properties.name: wow.log.partitions
properties.description: The partitions of each context's log: fixed once the log holds entries, a power of two that divides 4096 (decision D240), refused at start otherwise.

properties.name: wow.log.poll-interval
properties.description: How often a tail polls while it finds entries (finding A2-14).

properties.name: wow.log.store
properties.description: The store of every aggregate's log that `wow.aggregates.[<context>.<aggregate>].log.store` does not name (decision D177): one of `wow.stores`, the only one when not set.

properties.name: wow.mongo.append-timeout
properties.description: How long an append's insert may take on a store that sets none in its `options.append-timeout` (decision D261): below the default wait timeout, so a command appending during an outage is answered before its wait ends.

properties.name: wow.mongo.database
properties.description: The database of the log and the stores on the MongoDB backend.

properties.name: wow.node.address
properties.description: The `host:port` of this node's internal port, as the other nodes reach it.

properties.name: wow.node.id
properties.description: This node's id among the nodes of the service; a new one each start when not set.

properties.name: wow.schedules
properties.description: Per `@OnSchedule` job, by its name: `wow.schedules.<job>.*` (decision D198).

properties.name: wow.service
properties.description: The service's name; `spring.application.name` when not set.

properties.name: wow.snapshot.write-batch
properties.description: How many snapshots of a partition the snapshot subscriptions write together at most (decision D248 ②).

properties.name: wow.standby
properties.description: Whether the node starts on standby (design 07 §3, decision D32): through the dual-run window of a migration's cut-over it serves reads of what `migrate-data` imports, refuses every command (`wow.node.standby`, 503), and handles no subscription, retries no parked entry and runs no job, until its operator resumes it on the internal port (`POST /wow/node/resume` with the cluster token, naming who resumes it). A subscription that starts at the end of its stream starts where the stream ends at the resume.

properties.name: wow.state-cache.capacity
properties.description: The aggregate states kept per context between commands; 0 keeps none. Not set (the default), each context's cache is bounded by bytes instead (work package B.O-4): a tenth of the maximum heap (`-Xmx`), split between the node's contexts, each state weighed at an estimated 1 KB plus 12 bytes per recent request it holds (its rings grow with the requests the aggregate commits, up to `recent-requests`), and at least 4096 states with full rings. Most aggregates commit few requests, so the default holds several times as many of them as a count sized for full rings. A miss costs a snapshot and a tail read before the command is decided, so the cache should hold the aggregates written often: set a capacity when states are much larger than 1 KB (a capacity times the average state size should stay well within the heap). The `wow.state-cache` counter (`hit`, `miss`, `evicted`) shows the fit.

properties.name: wow.state-cache.recent-requests
properties.description: The requests each cached aggregate keeps of those it committed last, derived from the log (decision D261), so that most commands skip looking their request id up; 0 looks every request id up.

properties.name: wow.stores
properties.description: The named store instances (decision D177), by name: `wow.stores.<name>.type` and its settings.

properties.name: wow.subscriptions
properties.description: Per subscription, by its name (bracketed in a property name: `wow.subscriptions.[CartSaga.onOrderCreated]`).

properties.name: wow.tenant.default
properties.description: The tenant of a caller that has none, such as the anonymous one (decision D97).

properties.name: wow.topics.in-memory
properties.description: Whether the node's topics are in its JVM instead of Kafka.

properties.name: wow.wait.default-timeout
properties.description: How long a command whose request names no timeout waits (`Wow-Wait-Timeout`), whichever edge it came through: at most maxTimeout.

properties.name: wow.wait.max-hops
properties.description: The most hops of a wait plan, at most WaitOptions.MAX_HOPS_CAP; each saga a chain follows adds two.

properties.name: wow.wait.max-registered
properties.description: The most waits the node holds at once (review R3.4-3): beyond it a command whose plan waits past ACCEPTED is not run and is answered `wow.command.busy` (429, with `Retry-After`), FAILED at ACCEPTED.

properties.name: wow.wait.max-timeout
properties.description: The longest wait; a longer timeout is capped to it, and a node stops within it.

properties.name: wow.wait.unknown-contexts
properties.description: Whether a wait plan may name a context the node knows no Manifest of (decision D190): `allow`, checked where the chain arrives, or `reject`.
